title: cross edge vs forward edges of graphs

messages.content: cross edge vs forward edges of graphs

**Forward edge:** Non-tree edge `(u, v)` where `u` is an ancestor of `v` in the DFS tree (connects to a proper descendant). Timestamp ordering: `u.d < v.d < v.f < u.f`.

**Cross edge:** Any other edge — connects vertices where neither is an ancestor of the other (same tree but different branches, or different trees). Timestamp ordering: `v.d < v.f < u.d < u.f`.

In DFS, you distinguish them by color when exploring `(u, v)`:
- Target is **BLACK** and `u.d < v.d` → forward edge
- Target is **BLACK** and `u.d > v.d` → cross edge

In **undirected** graphs, neither forward nor cross edges exist (Theorem 20.10) — only tree edges and back edges.
